intro.author: Nahum the Elkoshite (1:1); his name means 'comfort,' and the location of Elkosh is unknown
intro.written: Between the fall of Thebes in 663 BC (3:8) and the fall of Nineveh in 612 BC
intro.audience: Judah, suffering under Assyrian domination, though much of the book addresses Nineveh
intro.setting: Assyria had ruled the Near East by terror for over a century. It destroyed Israel's northern kingdom in 722 BC, ravaged Judah in 701 BC and kept Judah as a tribute-paying vassal. Nineveh, its glittering capital, seemed unbeatable. In 612 BC an alliance of Babylonians and Medes destroyed it.
intro.purpose: To announce that God would judge Nineveh for its cruelty and arrogance, bringing comfort and relief to his oppressed people.
intro.bigIdea: 'The LORD is slow to anger, and great in power,' and no empire is beyond his justice.

outline.title: The Lord, avenger of his people and refuge for the faithful
